name: 민트 경차 (kei) facing left
label: jp_vehicles/jp-car-kei-mint/left
reasons: 화풍: 윤곽이 근흑(재질 어두운 톤 아님) (4/4)

answer.evidence: The van is a west-facing side view. Rows 6-15 form a wide, light roof plane with highlights. The silhouette widens from 40 to 59 px over rows 5-15, which suggests a foreshortened top. A 1-row darker edge line sits at row 16, followed by darker shadow at row 17, then the window band (rows 18-23) and the side body (rows 24-41) with wheels below. That gives about 25 rows of front face. The roof is a borderline read: it could also be a flat side-elevation panel, but the edge line and shadow below it count as evidence (a)/(c). The wheels are drawn in profile as part of the body.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a sage-green kei van in side view. Its body has about 4 lightness steps: a light roof highlight, a mid body tone, a darker lower panel and a dark shadow. Windows are flat dark blue-grey with a pale reflection streak. The main body panels and the roof are broad, smooth areas with little grain or panel texture. Measured facts: 88% of dark edge pixels are near-neutral, which matches the visible near-black/dark grey outline around the whole silhouette and the wheels, the sticker look. The references (hedge 0%, cheese stall 1%, well 33%) use tinted outlines. Visible tones per tile (9) match the hedge but fall well below the cheese stall (17) and the well (20). Near-flat coverage of 15% is slightly above the cheese stall (13%) and the hedge and well (0%), so there are flat fills on the door and body panels. The van is clean and readable, but it is shallower than the Beodeul standard in shading steps, outline tinting and surface texture.

surfaces.part: side body with windows and wheels (south face)

answer.evidence: The van is shown facing left, so its south face is the side profile with windows, door seams and two wheels at rows 17-41. Above that, a lighter roof band spans rows 6-15. The silhouette widens from 40 px at row 5 to 59 px at row 15, which suggests a receding top plane. The band ends in a darker front-edge line at row 16, and row 17 is a darker eave/shadow row before the window strip. That is a top surface of about 10 rows over a front face of about 25 rows.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a grey-green van with a dark outline all around the body and wheels. 88% of its dark edge pixels are near-neutral, so the outline is a uniform near-black line, the 'sticker' look. The references use tinted outlines (hedge 0%, stall 1%, well 33%). The body panels show about 3-4 lightness steps, with a light roof highlight and a dark lower band, against 5-6 on the references. The windows, doors and lower body are broad, smooth areas with little grain. Measured density is 9 visible tones per tile, matching the hedge but well below the stall (17) and the well (20). Near-flat coverage is 15%, close to the stall's 13%, but the references' 0% means the candidate has more flat fills. It is clean and readable, yet shallower than the references on shading steps, outline tinting and surface texture.

surfaces.part: upper body / roof panel above windows

answer.evidence: The van is drawn as a pure side elevation. The large light-green block at rows 6-15 is a flat panel with a dithered sheen highlight. Its tone is uniform (L=153) down to a 2-row darker band at rows 16-17, which is a window frame rather than a front-edge line with eave shadow. It has no ellipse and no separate roof plane, and the silhouette widens only through the slanted windshield and rear corner. Below it come the windows (rows 18-23), the door and body panel (rows 24-37) and the wheels. No horizontal top surface is visible, so this is a side profile without a top.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a sage-green van with a body ramp of about 3 steps (base, a lighter roof/top highlight, a darker lower body), glass of 2-3 tones, and dark wheels. The measured facts show 88% of its dark edge pixels are near-neutral, which fits a uniform near-black outline around the body, windows and wheels. That is the sticker look. Beodeul references such as the hedge, cheese stall and well use tinted outlines, at 0%, 1% and 33% near-neutral. The side panels and the lower body are large, mostly flat areas, and the 15% near-flat coverage matches this. Texture is limited to a few dither dots on the roof and the hood. The 9 visible tones per tile equal the hedge but sit well below the stall (17) and the well (20). The shading is shallower than the references and the outline is not material-toned, so a careful artist would not accept it next to them.

The roof is only weakly separated from the body, but the edge line and the clear step in lightness between roof and body make it count as a top surface.
